Descrivi la lesione e indica che tipo di: Describe the lesion and indicate which type of tumor is most likely.
Lesione infiltrante, iperintensa in T2/F:
Infiltrating lesion, hyperintense on T2/FLAIR, without enhancement, in a young adult: low-grade diffuse glioma. According to WHO 2021, adult diffuse gliomas are distinguished by their molecular profile: IDH-mutant astrocytoma (1p/19q intact), IDH-mutant and 1p/19q-codeleted oligodendroglioma, IDH wild-type glioblastoma.
Clues for oligodendroglioma: frontal or insular cortical-subcortical location, less sharp margins, heterogeneous T2 signal, calcifications (better seen on CT or SWI). Clue for IDH-mutant astrocytoma with intact 1p/19q: the "T2-FLAIR mismatch" sign (lesion homogeneous on T2 with a hypointense center on FLAIR and a hyperintense rim). The definitive diagnosis remains histologic and molecular.
The absence of enhancement does not exclude grade 3: enhancement is often, but not always, present in higher-grade gliomas.
Lesione cerebrale senza impregnazione in: Non-enhancing brain lesion in a young person: low-grade glioma; the type is told by the molecular profile.
Oligodendroglioma, IDH-mutato e 1p/19q c: Oligodendroglioma, IDH-mutant and 1p/19q-codeleted, WHO grade 2 (data from the ReMIND collection).
